chitchat: This is the gate. You're outside it.
I'm not going to make you leave. I'm going to not let you in.
Look at the road for a bit. It's a good road.
Two hours on, four off. It isn't a bad shift.
You want me to say something frightening. I would rather not.
The masks are for the road. This is the gate.
description:
She's standing in the gate house door because she's too tall for the gate house, and she has to duck to get into her own guardroom, and she does it eleven times a shift without appearing to notice.

Her left arm is longer than her right by most of a forearm and ends in a hand with too many bones in it. She uses it to reach things down off high shelves without moving her feet, and to hold you at a distance that's exactly out of your reach and exactly inside hers, and she's doing the second one now.

She isn't hostile. She isn't going to move either.

bye.text:
"Right."

And they go back to it, which out here is the whole of a goodbye.

city.text:
She considers the question like it's a piece of work.

"I went to Coldwater when I was nineteen. Got to the checkpoint at the Yards. There's a frame there you walk through and a man behind glass who reads what it says about you."

A pause, and she looks down the road rather than at you.

"He wasn't cruel about it. That's the bit people get wrong. He was bored. He had done it forty times that day and I was the forty-first and he didn't look up."

She rolls her shoulder, the long one.

"Anyway. Nothing to tell. Everyone here has that story and everyone here is bored of it."

in.text:
She nods once, and doesn't congratulate you, and doesn't smile.

"Good enough."

And she puts her long hand flat against the thorn, and the thorn draws back off the frame, all along its length, without hurrying and without any sound worth the word, and stays back.

"Gate is open to you. Eat at the Fire, the food is free and you'll feel strange about that for a fortnight. Don't go in the Fleshery. Don't touch a rack in the Milkhouse. Everything else in there you can walk into and somebody will tell you what it is."

She turns back to the road.

"And when they ask you what you were before, tell them. They won't care and you won't believe that until it has happened about four times."

options.label: You don't think much of the Basin.

masks.text:
"The road works."

She almost smiles, and it's the first thing in the conversation she has plainly enjoyed.

"You came up it. You're here and you're being polite to me. It works."

And she doesn't say another word about it, and doesn't offer to explain what's on the road, and there's something about the way she stopped that suggests the explanation would be very boring indeed.

out.text:
"Right."

She doesn't look disappointed. She looks like somebody who has just had a question answered honestly and is filing it.

"That's a real answer and I would rather have it than the other thing. Bracken owes you and Bracken pays, so you won't go short out here."

She settles back against the frame.

"But no. Not through here. Ask me again if that ever changes."

root.first: "Stop there." She doesn't raise her voice and doesn't need to. "You have come a long way and you're going to be told no, so I'll tell you fast and you can decide what to do with the afternoon."

options.label: You don't think much of the Basin.
Is there anything I could do?

text_by_relation.close: "Come in out of the sun a minute," she says, and stands aside from a doorway you still can't use.
text_by_relation.familiar: "There you are." She reaches something down off a shelf without looking at it. "Still outside. For now."
text_by_relation.known: "You again." She shifts, and the gate house door frame creaks. "Still outside."

toll.text:
She looks at you for a long moment, and something in it changes, and it isn't warmth. It's that she has decided to stop being professional at you.

"All right. Yes. There is."

She points west with her chin, out over the flats.

"One of Bracken's bitches went out four days ago and hasn't come back and she's heavy in whelp. He has been out three nights and he's fifty-one and he'll kill himself doing it and he won't stop. Go and find her and bring her in."

"She won't come to you. Just find her and stay with her and she'll follow you when she has decided about you. It'll take as long as it takes."

A pause.

"And no, this isn't a test, and no, I'm not going to let you in for it. I'm asking because I have got a gate to stand at and you have got legs."

options.label: Whatever it turns out I need it to be.
Keep it exactly as it is.

toll_done.text:
Bracken Hale came down the road at a run, which at fifty-one he shouldn't have done, and took the animal off you without a word, and hasn't come back out.

Quarrel Nine watched all of it from the gate and hasn't said anything for some time.

She takes her time about it. "Right." "I'm going to ask you one thing and then I'm going to do something about it, and I want you to actually think, because people say the easy answer here and then they're inside and it's a problem for everybody."

She turns round and looks down at you.

"What are you going to do with your body?"

toll_no.text:
"Fair enough."

And she means it, entirely, and goes back to watching the road, and the conversation is over in a way that leaves nothing at all to push against.

toll_take.text:
"West and south. Past the Rise, keep off the high ground, you'll hear her before you see her."

She goes back to watching the road, and then, without turning round: "Take water. Two. One of them isn't for you."

options.label: You don't think much of the Basin.

why.text:
"Because of what happened the last four times."

She says it without any heat at all.

"Twice it was Ascendant survey crews with a paper saying this land was theirs. Once it was a Long Watch pair who wanted to count us. Once it was a man on his own who was exactly as harmless as you look and came back in the spring with eleven friends and a truck."

"So. No. It isn't about you. It has never once been about the person standing where you're standing."

a shirt with the left sleeve gone entirely

name: Quarrel Nine
